newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire aid mission finds thousands more refugees.
newsitem.headline: Zaire aid mission finds thousands more refugees.

text.p: An aid mission to an area of eastern Zaire not visited by United Nations officials for weeks has discovered thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees, many on the verge of death, U.N. officials said on Sunday.
Aid officials who travelled by rail to Ubolo village south of Kisangani distributed 26 tonnes of food before leaving with 468 refugees, mainly children.

"We found about 5,000 to 6,000 refugees near a village at kilometre 82 (50 miles) south of Kisangani," said Julian Fleet, a U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) official who led the mission. "Many people have died there and many more are on the verge of death."

The mission reached Ubolo on Saturday night and returned to Kisangani on Sunday evening. Aid workers had to carry most of the refugees off the train to a ferry crossing the Zaire river as they were too weak to walk.
"The local Zaireans have cared for them as best they could, but this is absolutely an emergency situation," said Fleet.
Fleet said the refugees mobbed the train when it arrived at the village, with thousands pleading for food or begging to be taken out.

Many could not walk and were crawling toward the train, he said. One refugee emerging from the forest a few kilometers from the village lay across the tracks and refused to move until he was promised passage home.
"We also saw a lot more refugees in the forest, trying for the train as we passed," said Fleet.

Aid workers have been barred from travelling further than 41 kms (25 miles) south of Kisangani by Zairean rebels who now control the bulk of the country. Rebel soldiers sealed off the area after attacks on Biaro camp, about 41 kms (25 miles) south of Kisangani which refugees blamed on local Zaireans and rebel soldiers.
Over 80,000 refugees fled Biaro and nearby Kasese camps after the attacks -- including those now at Ubolo, aid officials said.
The refugees are the remnants of nearly two million Hutus who fled Rwanda in 1994 to escape reprisal for the genocide of up to 800.000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
U.N. officials said on Sunday hundreds of Rwandan Hutu refugees have made their way almost 1,500 km (900 miles) across the breadth of Zaire and have begun appearing in the Congo.

UNHCR spkesman Peter Kessler said 50 refugees had been seen at Loukolela, 350 kms (200 miles) northeast of Brazzaville. He said a western missionary at Liranga, 50 kms (30 miles) further east, reported over 2,600 refugee arrivals in the past few days.
"We had a team confirm the Loukolela arrivals and hope to do the same for Liranga in the next day or so," Kessler told Reuters.
To have reached this point, the refugees have cut through some of the most dense forest on earth and traversed scores of rivers in their eight-month trek.

Scores of refugees on Sunday began arriving at Biaro Camp, about 41 kms (25 miles) south of Kisangani, in the hope of joining a U.N. airlift back to Rwanda. The new arrivals said they had walked from Ubundu, over 100 kms (65 miles) further south, after hearing the airlift had finally got underway.
One man, his foot broken from what he said was an attack by Zairean villagers, had limped almost the whole way while carrying his daughter.

The U.N. airlift continued on Sunday with nearly 2,000 more flying home, bringing the total since it began on April 27 to over 18,000. U.N. officials hope to complete an airlift of the remaining 25,000 refugees at Biaro camp within 10 days.
Aid organisations believe over 200,000 refugees are still unaccounted for, but Rwandan officials insist only around 55,000 remain.
